title: Somalia: Issues and Options in the Energy Sector
venue_or_publisher: Joint UNDP/World Bank Energy Sector Assessment Program, Report 5796-SO
data_period: November–December 1984 mission; historical series and scenarios to 1995
method: Multidisciplinary assessment mission, energy balances, engineering/economic appraisal and policy recommendations.
data_sources: Mission observations, utility/petroleum agency records and earlier studies.
key_findings: Identifies vehicle maintenance, driving practice and mass transport as fuel-saving routes; integrates petroleum procurement with electricity, household fuels and industry.
limitations: Historical institutions, prices and infrastructure are not a current baseline; savings are recommendations or estimates, not evaluated interventions.
project_relevance: Historical whole-energy-system framing and fuel-balance provenance.
verification_locator: Cover; mission note PDF p6; printed pp29–30 (paras2.24–2.26); chapterIV contents.
quality_appraisal: Useful contemporaneous baseline; no transfer of 1980 s coefficients into present scenarios.
data_code_availability: Tables in report; machine-readable model/code not inspected.

title: Are They Predisposed to the Resources Curse? Oil in Somalia
venue_or_publisher: International Journal of Energy Economics and Policy 5(1), 231–245
data_period: Historical discussion through approximately 2014; exact search cutoff not reported
method: Documentary case study explicitly excluding new primary data collection.
data_sources: Archival records, academic articles, institutional and NGO reports.
key_findings: Argues that weak institutions and contested resource rights create petroleum-governance risks; proposes stronger institutions and local participation.
limitations: No original interviews or causal estimate; quoted resource potential is not proof of commercially recoverable reserves.
project_relevance: Trace resource-curse arguments to their evidentiary basis.
verification_locator: Journal title page p231; section8, pp238–239; analysis and concluding discussion.
quality_appraisal: Transparent admission of secondary-data limits; useful framing, weak basis for production or revenue calibration.
data_code_availability: References provided; no empirical dataset/code identified.

title: Somalia Transport Sector Needs Assessment and Investment Programme
geographic_scope: Somalia; scope includes ports, aviation and road corridors
data_period: Planning baseline circa 2015–2016; ten-year investment horizon
method: Demand/network planning using city populations, available traffic counts and trade estimates, according to official government synopsis.
data_sources: AfDB assessment summarized by Somalia Investment Promotion Office.
key_findings: Provides an earlier transport planning baseline linking transport demand, corridors and investment priorities.
limitations: Full AfDB PDF inaccessible in this run. Findings restricted to official synopsis; do not treat its historical network description as current.
project_relevance: Retrieve detailed traffic-count and route assumptions before transport-energy modeling.
verification_locator: SOMINVEST Transport & Infrastructure, opening assessment paragraphs: https://sominvest.gov.so/key-sectors/transport-infrastructure/ .
quality_appraisal: Government synopsis verifies relevance and methodology; full underlying assessment remains to be inspected.
data_code_availability: Report linked; no raw traffic observations/code acquired.

title: The Initial National Communication for Somalia to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
authors: Office of the Prime Minister, Federal Republic of Somalia
geographic_scope: Somalia national estimates; petroleum proxies drawn from Somaliland and Puntland
data_period: 1990–2015 inventory; scenarios to 2040; publication August 2018, registry submission January 2019
method: IPCC Tier 1 inventory plus sectoral baseline/mitigation scenarios.
data_sources: AFREC, earlier reports and Somaliland/Puntland energy statistics; surrogate data where disaggregation missing.
key_findings: Explicitly reports high petroleum-data uncertainty and proxy use; transport options include maintenance, road improvements and mass transit.
limitations: National extrapolation from subnational data is an assumption. Imports and fuel-use definitions conflict; numerical totals require reconciliation.
project_relevance: Find the assumptions behind inherited fuel and transport emissions baselines.
verification_locator: Printed pp108–110, sections4.3.2–4.3.2.1; pp116–119 transport; cover visually inspected.
quality_appraisal: Valuable provenance disclosure; unsuitable as unqualified observed national fuel consumption.
data_code_availability: Tabular estimates supplied; underlying microdata or executable model not identified.

title: Oil and Gas in the Political Marketplace in Somalia
venue_or_publisher: London School of Economics and Political Science, Conflict Research Programme
geographic_scope: Somalia federal and regional petroleum politics
method: Qualitative political-economy analysis combining remote and Mogadishu key-informant interviews with documents.
data_sources: Somali analysts, aid specialists, present/former officials, businesses and oil experts; legislation and reports.
key_findings: Finds anticipated rents and subcontracting opportunities shape institutional bargaining before commercial extraction; transparency and federal coordination matter.
limitations: Purposive expert evidence does not quantify economy-wide effects; 2020 assessment cannot establish current contracts or recoverable reserves.
project_relevance: Design realistic governance and financing scenarios for energy projects.
verification_locator: PDF p2 para3 (39 interviews); pp11–13 conclusions and outstanding regulatory issues.
quality_appraisal: Original interviews provide stronger contextual evidence than purely secondary resource-curse essays; sensitive claims need triangulation.
data_code_availability: Interview transcripts not supplied in inspected report.

title: Somalia Country Environmental Analysis: Diagnostic Study on Trends and Threats for Environmental and Natural Resources Challenges
method: Environmental diagnostic with projected fleet growth and vehicle-emission coefficients.
data_sources: Earlier transport assessment; continental growth assumption; US EPA passenger-vehicle factors and author assumptions for trucks/buses.
key_findings: Estimates rising road-transport emissions, using assumed fleet growth, fuel economy and mileage. These are projections, not a Somali vehicle-emissions survey.
limitations: Assumes 6.5% annual fleet growth and borrowed vehicle factors; national fleet composition/activity need validation.
project_relevance: Identify inherited transport-emission assumptions and replace them with local measurements.
verification_locator: Printed pp94–95; Figures29–30 and footnotes102–103; p95 visually inspected.
quality_appraisal: Assumptions are recoverable and reviewable; local external validity is limited.
data_code_availability: Figures and assumptions available; raw fleet survey/code not identified.

title: Somalia’s First Biennial Update Report to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
authors: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, Federal Republic of Somalia
publication_type: official national inventory and mitigation report
data_period: Inventory 2000–2020; mitigation scenarios to 2030; September 2022 report, UNFCCC submission April 2023
method: IPCC inventory and LEAP baseline/mitigation modeling; consultations and expert interviews.
data_sources: UN statistics for transport fuels; historical sector data and policy assumptions.
key_findings: Already uses LEAP across energy sectors. Transport analysis is top-down because fleet mileage and fuel-economy data are inadequate.
limitations: GDP-led fuel projections and assumed policy savings are scenarios; model files not located. Inventory/mitigation vintage differences need care.
project_relevance: Essential prior work before claiming a first Somalia energy model; explicit lead to missing transport inputs.
verification_locator: Printed p105 section3.2.3; pp134–135 section3.3.3.2; pp162–163 data constraints.
quality_appraisal: Clear method and data-gap disclosure; policy scenarios are not measured outcomes.
data_code_availability: Charts, assumptions and references present; LEAP project/code not linked in inspected sections.

title: Commodified Cities: Urbanization and Public Goods in Somalia
geographic_scope: Mogadishu, Kismayo, Beledweyne, Baidoa, Galkayo, Bosaso and Borama; source preserves Somaliland/Puntland distinctions
data_period: Underlying studies prepared for 2020 Somalia Urbanization Review; exact fieldwork dates not established
method: Synthesis of literature, seven city studies and a political-economy synthesis on public goods.
data_sources: Nine commissioned studies, including unpublished empirical city material.
key_findings: Mobility costs and spatial access differ by wealth, displacement and gender; private transport provision does not assure inclusive access.
limitations: Not a representative national travel or energy-use survey; some gender/mode observations are explicitly anecdotal.
project_relevance: Include affordability, service geography and livelihoods in transport transition assessment.
verification_locator: Methods pp12–13; mobility pp53–61; conclusion pp62–64.
quality_appraisal: Useful multi-city contextual evidence; no direct vehicle energy intensities or measured modal shift.
data_code_availability: Source references available; underlying nine studies not all publicly attached.

title: Challenges of post-conflict urban transportation reconstruction in Mogadishu, Somalia
venue_or_publisher: Physics and Chemistry of the Earth, Parts A/B/C 129,103307
data_period: Publication 2023; underlying data dates not established from abstract
method: Assessment of challenges/opportunities for Mogadishu City Transport Planning Approach; detailed methods inaccessible.
key_findings: Identifies insufficient transport planning statistics and examines post-conflict reconstruction challenges.
limitations: Only institutional-repository abstract inspected; sample, validation and numerical findings not assessed.
project_relevance: Transport-planning citation lead, not a verified transport-energy parameter source.
verification_locator: Author-institution abstract PDF pp1–2: https://umpir.ump.edu.my/id/eprint/35781/7/Challenges%20of%20post-conflict%20urban%20transportation%20reconstruction%20in%20Mogadishu.pdf ; journal metadata in repository35781.
quality_appraisal: Bibliography verified; methodological confidence cannot be rated from abstract alone.
data_code_availability: Full article restricted at institution; public two-page PDF contains abstract/acknowledgements only.

title: Urban Mobility Complexities in Mogadishu
publication_type: research-organization commentary based on public forum
method: Stakeholder forum synthesis and referenced contextual analysis.
data_sources: Urban practitioners, businesspeople, students, teachers, car owners, lawyers and security analysts; sample size not stated.
key_findings: Security closures, weak traffic management and limited bus services constrain mobility; recommends accessible collective transport and coordination.
limitations: Forum is not representative; no fuel-economy, traffic-count or causal policy evaluation supplied.
project_relevance: Account for route restrictions, occupancy and livelihood implications when studying electric three-wheelers.
verification_locator: Main article: forum description; causes; contributing factors; recommendations.
quality_appraisal: Local stakeholder perspective adds context; counts attributed to other sources need independent checking.
data_code_availability: References linked; forum transcripts/data not supplied.

title: Creating Markets in Somalia: Unlocking Private Sector-Led Growth at a Critical Juncture of Somalia’s Development
data_period: Evidence assembled before June 2024; mixed source years
method: Expert/key-informant interviews, secondary review and qualitative sector diagnostics.
data_sources: Private-sector stakeholders, official statistics, surveys and institutional reports.
key_findings: Identifies transport/logistics, regulation, finance and electricity as linked investment constraints; enactment of electricity law had not ensured effective implementation.
limitations: Directional diagnosis in a data-poor setting, not a causal impact evaluation; not a statement of 2026 legal status.
project_relevance: Sequence infrastructure investment with enforceable rules, finance and service competition.
verification_locator: Cover June2024 and copyright; executive summary pIV; transport pp48–51; electricity pp72–81; finance pp82–98.
quality_appraisal: Strong source mapping and explicit data limits; avoid treating all borrowed statistics as contemporaneous.
data_code_availability: References present; interview microdata not attached.

title: Energy Transition Assessment: Somalia
geographic_scope: Somalia national policy; local project illustrations
data_period: Published June 2025; mixed historical evidence and 2030 proposals
method: Stakeholder-informed transition diagnosis and policy action plan.
data_sources: Government engagement, validation workshop and cited institutional energy sources.
key_findings: Recommends operational regulation, finance and skills; suggests renewable-charged captive EV pilots given high upfront costs and diesel electricity constraints.
limitations: EV, biofuel and hydrogen proposals are not field-tested performance results. Fossil-fuel allocation statement needs reconciliation with older assessments.
project_relevance: Integrate transport and productive demand into policy scenarios, with pilot evidence before scaling.
verification_locator: Executive summary pp9–11; transport p22; finance pp23–24; action plan pp37–44.
quality_appraisal: Useful current policy synthesis; no transparent bottom-up national transport fleet model.
data_code_availability: Report references; no replicable transport model or pilot dataset identified.

title: Updated Somalia’s Third Generation Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0)
authors: Ministry of Environment and Climate Change, Federal Republic of Somalia
method: National policy targets and sector priorities; underlying modeling not inspected in current run.
data_sources: UNFCCC registry and NDC Partnership official country synopsis.
key_findings: Commits to 34% below business-as-usual GHG emissions by 2035, including energy, transport and cooling priorities.
limitations: Official summary only: full updated PDF could not be retrieved in this run; no sector-specific arithmetic or assumptions audited here.
project_relevance: Policy scenario reference; targets must remain separate from measured outcomes.
verification_locator: UNFCCC Somalia registry lists8September2025; NDC Partnership country overview: https://ndcpartnership.org/country/som .
quality_appraisal: Reliable for declared commitment and scope; insufficient for calibration or allocation of national cap to electricity.
data_code_availability: Full PDF public URL supplied; current-run access limitation recorded.

title: Oil and peace: assessing the impact of Somalia–Türkiye hydrocarbon cooperation on post-conflict stability and national sovereignty
geographic_scope: Somalia; contextual comparison with South Sudan, Libya and Angola
data_period: 2024 agreement; article 1 April 2026; documentary cutoff not clearly specified
method: Interpretive documentary case study and thematic analysis.
data_sources: Legal/policy instruments, official/institutional reports, academic literature and some media.
key_findings: Frames hydrocarbon cooperation as conditional opportunity with risks of centralization, elite capture and external dependency.
limitations: No original outcome measurement or counterfactual; public-document and reported-contract claims require legal-source verification.
project_relevance: Contrast recent governance narratives with older interview evidence.
verification_locator: Abstract; section3 methodology; sections4–5; data-availability statement.
quality_appraisal: Analytical risk framing, not proof that specified effects occurred or that commercial resources exist.
data_code_availability: Article says original contributions included in article/supplement; no coded source corpus verified.

title: Mogadishu – National Coordination Meeting Minutes, 17 March 2026
geographic_scope: Somalia operational network; Mogadishu, Puntland and Somaliland differences noted
data_period: March 2026; meeting 17 March, file name 18 March
method: Operational coordination report citing a 46-respondent retailer/transport survey and partner updates.
data_sources: WFP/Logistics Cluster survey and humanitarian operational partners.
key_findings: Reports fuel-price and supply disruptions affecting transport, generators and water trucking, with geographic differences.
limitations: Sampling/units incomplete; jet-fuel percentage contradicts its printed prices. Do not import the displayed rates as verified national price statistics.
project_relevance: Lead for supplier surveys and fuel-shock scenarios; retain the original date and unresolved errors.
verification_locator: PDF pp1–5; section4 p4 visually inspected.
quality_appraisal: Timely operational signal but small unspecified sample and internal arithmetic error limit calibration.
data_code_availability: Survey instrument/raw responses not attached; follow-on market assessment mentioned.

title: Somalia National Electricity Act 2023
authors: Ministry of Energy and Water Resources, Federal Republic of Somalia
method: Official announcement summarizing statutory institutions and intended functions.
data_sources: Ministry publication; linked legal text not analyzed.
key_findings: Confirms enactment and proposed regulatory architecture, including National Electricity Authority and licensing/tariff functions.
limitations: Announcement is not evidence of enforcement or improved access; full legal text and later amendments not reviewed.
project_relevance: Prevent outdated blanket claims that Somalia has no electricity legislation.
verification_locator: Page title and announcement dated 8 March 2023; measures and National Electricity Authority paragraphs. Legal PDF not analyzed.
quality_appraisal: Primary source for enactment, limited for implementation assessment.
data_code_availability: Linked Somali Electricity Act PDF; no implementation dataset.

title: Transport starter data kit: Historical passenger and freight transport data for selected countries in Africa, Asia, and South America
publication_type: peer-reviewed data article with linked dataset
geographic_scope: 60 countries; Somalia explicitly confirmed in Table 5 and master Zenodo record
data_period: 1990–2021 where available; dataset v1.4 December 2023; article online October 2024
method: Secondary compilation with observation-status codes, assumptions and country links.
data_sources: World Bank, UN DESA, IRF and other sources; African energy intensities/load factors borrowed from South Africa.
key_findings: Provides a Somalia-specific transport data starting point; country inclusion is confirmed, but the Somalia workbook contents were not inspected.
limitations: Missing, deprecated and discrepant observations acknowledged. Regional proxy intensities are not Somali measurements; unit definitions require checking.
project_relevance: Audit the Somalia workbook before designing new demand data collection.
verification_locator: Article sections 2–3, Limitations and Table 5; Table 5 Somalia DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7998431. Master dataset v1.4: https://zenodo.org/records/10406893 .
quality_appraisal: Transparent assumptions and reusable structure; country-specific completeness remains unaudited.
data_code_availability: Master TSDK_ALL.xlsx listed at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10406893; Somalia DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7998431. Workbook not downloaded in this review. Current concept DOI resolves to version10.5281/zenodo.10409827; two-file listing verified, workbook contents not inspected.
